title: The 2nd step of the “step base” algorithm for the “input” element seems to be wrong
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The 2nd step of the “step base” algorithm at https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-min-zero states this requirement:

> If the element has a [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-value) content attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-value) content attribute is not an error, then return that result.

But even just on the face of it, that step doesn’t appear to make much sense — given that the purpose of the “step base” algorithm is to compute a floor/base against which the `value` (parsed into an actual number) is evaluated.

Compare that 2nd step to the 1st step, which is to use the value of the `min` attribute, and the step, which is to use the “default step base”, if there is one, and especially to the 4th (fall-through) step, which is to just return zero.

Those 1st, 3rd, and 4th steps _do_ make sense in the context of them being a floor/base against which the `value` value is evaluated.

Especially “zero” (the 4th-step fall-through) is kind of intuitively obvious as floor/base. And in the context of zero as the fall-through, the idea of the `value` value itself otherwise being the floor/base seems pretty odd.

That is, evaluating the `value` value against _itself_ — which is what the 2nd step seems to require, doesn’t appear to make much sense.

And that’s further attested to if you consider the “Constraint validation” algorithm at https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-step-attribute:concept-input-value-string-number-3 for determining of the element is “suffering from a step mismatch”:

> Constraint validation: When the element has an [allowed value step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-step), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element's [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-fe-value) is a number, and that number subtracted from the [step base](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-min-zero) is not an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-step), the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#suffering-from-a-step-mismatch).

Specifically: For any element that has no `min` attribute, then we‘re going to hit the 2nd step of that “step base” algorithm. Which means the “step base” value will be the same as the `value` value. And so then, the result of subtracting that `value` value from the “step base” value is _always_ going to be zero. And no matter what the “allowed value step” may be, zero is always going to be an integral multiple of it.

But if the 2nd step of that “step base” algorithm is removed, then the “step base” algorithm is going to most often be returning zero. And then, for any non-zero `value` value, the result of subtracting that `value` value from zero is always going to be some non-zero number. And that makes sense.

And finally, in my implementation: If I drop the 2nd step of that “step base” algorithm, then I get passes for the relevant tests at http://wpt.live/html/semantics/forms/constraints/form-validation-reportValidity.html.

But if I _don’t_ drop that 2nd step — and instead strictly follow the current spec requirements as written — then I get failures for all the relevant tests.
